ActionBinding.description:
One declared mutation: a host action primitive, the reader binding whose kind it acts on, the arguments that fix what it writes, and what must be true of the object before it is written.

Flux and Argo CD declare their actions using this contract in API 0.3.

arguments.description: What this action writes, fixed at install time.

availableWhen.description:
What must be true of the object for the control to be offered. The same predicates, asked by the surface rather than by the cluster request, so a person is not shown a button whose refusal is already known.

Display only, and deliberately so: an app that needs a condition *enforced* declares it in `preconditions`, where the host is what checks it. A surface can be out of date; the fresh GET cannot.

preconditions.description:
What must be true of the object for the write to be sent. Evaluated by the host against the fresh GET the primitive already performs, before the patch; a predicate that does not hold refuses the request and the operator is told this predicate's `reason`.

These add refusals. The host's own guards — an object being deleted, a UID or `resourceVersion` that has moved — run first and are not something a manifest can reach.

resource.description: The name of a reader binding in `capabilities`. The action acts on that binding's kind and on no other.

Badge.description: A word on a built-in row. Without a `join`, the rules read the row's own `.metadata`; with one, they read the joined custom resource. The first rule that holds is the badge; when none does there is no badge.

join.description: A declared join whose matched resource the rules read.

jsonPath.description: A value shown beside each row, and what rows are ordered by; by namespace and name when absent.

limit.description: How many rows to show, 1–10; by the card's size when absent.

jsonPath.description: A number on each object, in the predicates' bounded path grammar.

CardPredicate.description:
What a dashboard card counts (#540): one question about one value of each object its source lists.

The action predicates' path grammar, literal rule and `equals` / `absent`, plus two date operators. There is no `reason`: nothing is refused, so there is nothing to tell an operator. Exactly one operator per predicate:

```json {"jsonPath": ".status.notAfter", "within": "14d"} ```

absent.description: `true`: the value at `jsonPath` must be unset or null.

before.description: The value at `jsonPath` is an RFC 3339 timestamp earlier than now plus this duration: `14d` includes everything already past, `0d` is only the past, `-30d` is older than thirty days.

equals.description: The value at `jsonPath` must equal this string, number or boolean.

jsonPath.description: The value this predicate asks about, in the same bounded JSONPath subset as an action predicate's.

within.description: The value at `jsonPath` is an RFC 3339 timestamp within this duration of now: `14d` is from now until fourteen days ahead, `-1h` the last hour. Units s, m, h, d and w.

CardSize.description: How much of the dashboard's width a card takes.

page.description: The `id` of a page in `contributions.pages` that lists the card's source.

oneOf.description: How many objects the predicate holds for.
Those objects counted by the status the app's status resolver gives them (#541).
One number reduced from a value of those objects.
The first few of those objects.

CommandTarget.description: What a palette command does: exactly one of opening a declared page or running a declared action through the host's confirmation.

oneOf.description: The `name` of a declared action in `actions`.

Condition.description:
One question about one value, without a sentence to say when it fails.

A [`Predicate`] is a condition plus the reason an operator is told when it does not hold. A status rule (#541) asks which of its rules describes an object; nobody is refused, so there is no reason to give — but the operators, the paths and the evaluation are these, and are this code:

```json {"jsonPath": ".spec.suspend", "equals": true} ```

absent.description: `true`: the value at `jsonPath` must be unset or null.

equals.description: The value at `jsonPath` must equal this literal.

jsonPath.description: The value this condition asks about, in the grammar [`resolve`] documents.

notEquals.description: The value at `jsonPath` must not equal this literal. An unset field is not equal to anything, so this holds when it is absent.

present.description: `true`: the value at `jsonPath` must be set and not null.

selfReference.description: The value at `jsonPath` must be a reference, in this host-known format, to the very object the rule reads. See [`ReferenceFormat`].

badges.description: Words an app puts on built-in rows, from the row's metadata or from a joined resource (#541).

commands.description: Entries in the command palette (#544): open one of this app's pages, or run one of its declared actions on the resource the reader has open.

statusResolvers.description: What status an app's custom resources have (#541). Replaces `pages[].statusColumns`, which is deprecated but still accepted in 0.3.

DashboardCard.description: A card on the cluster dashboard: one figure about the objects one granted custom-resource reader lists, drawn by the host.

list.description: How a `list` card orders and bounds its rows; refused on other types.

metric.description: What a `metric` card reads; required there and refused elsewhere.

predicate.description: Which of the source's objects the card counts; every one when absent.

source.description: The name of a `k8s.listCustomResource` binding in `capabilities`.

target.description: The app page the card opens, with the predicate applied as its filter.

title.description: Untrusted display text, drawn as plain text.

DetailLink.description: An entry in a resource detail view's app links menu that opens a read-only results panel. It never writes to the cluster; the name `rowActions` is reserved for declared mutations.

Join.description: A single granted custom-resource list used to enrich native table rows.

ManifestKind.description: Only data is executable in this first host. Code-bearing manifests must go through the future sandboxed runtime, never through a permissive fallback.

NormalizedStatus.description: The six statuses every surface knows how to draw.

PaletteCommand.description: One command palette entry. The host shows it under the app's name, so an app cannot pass its command off as the host's own.

forKinds.description: For an action command: the qualified kinds it is offered on, which must be the kind of the reader binding its action acts on. A page command has no subject and takes none.

Predicate.description:
One declared check about the object an action would write.

Exactly one operator per predicate:

```json {"jsonPath": ".spec.suspend", "notEquals": true, "reason": "Resume this resource before requesting reconciliation"} ```

absent.description: `true`: the value at `jsonPath` must be unset or null.

equals.description: The value at `jsonPath` must equal this literal.

jsonPath.description: The value this predicate asks about, as a bounded JSONPath subset: `.spec.suspend`, `.metadata.annotations['acme.io/pinned']`, `.status.conditions[0].status`. The grammar is the bounded subset the module documents: no wildcard or recursive descent, and one filter form, `[?(@.type=="Ready")]`, that selects the first matching element.

notEquals.description: The value at `jsonPath` must not equal this literal. An unset field is not equal to anything, so this holds when it is absent.

present.description: `true`: the value at `jsonPath` must be set and not null.

reason.description: What the operator is told when this predicate does not hold. Untrusted display text: written by the app, and escaped by the host before anything draws it.

ReferenceFormat.description:
A reference format the host knows how to check against the object that carries it (#541 review).

A condition compares against literals, so it cannot say "this annotation names the resource it is on". An ownership claim needs exactly that — a copied annotation must not make a resource look owned — so the host implements the check for each format, exactly as the owning controller does, rather than offering a template language.

oneOf.description: Argo CD's resource tracking id, `<app>:<group>/<kind>:<namespace>/<name>`, parsed as Argo CD parses it (`util/argo/resource_tracking.go`, `ParseAppInstanceValue`) and held to the resource as Argo CD holds it (`controller/state.go`, `isSelfReferencedObj`): group, kind and name equal, and namespace equal unless the resource is cluster-scoped. Argo CD ignores an id that does not name its own resource, so a badge must.

StatusResolver.description: Ordered rules that resolve the status of the custom resources of `forKinds`. The first rule whose conditions all hold is the status; when none does the host says `unknown`.

forKinds.description: Qualified kinds of custom resources this app declares a reader for.

StatusRule.description: One rule: when every condition holds, the object has this status.

label.description: The word shown. Required: colour is never the only signal.

reason.description: Where in the object the reason is, e.g. `.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Ready")].message`.

when.description: Every condition must hold. An empty list always holds, which is how a last, catch-all rule is written.

$schema.description: Editor metadata: the JSON Schema the manifest is written against. The host ignores it; it is the one key allowed that is not part of the contract.

actions.description: Declared mutations (#549). Absent in a manifest that only reads, and left out of the serialized form when empty so a manifest stored and signed without it still round-trips to its own bytes.
